# Use audience-profile

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Translate an audience type (exec, board, technical, sales, investor, internal, partner, customer) into structural rules — slide count, density, tone, must-have sections, things to avoid. Reusable across deck-builder, slide-outliner, and exec-summary.

**Reach for it when** Use whenever a stakeholder communication deliverable is being designed for a specific audience.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install audience-profile                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install audience-profile --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install audience-profile --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Stakeholder comms pack: [`--pack stakeholder-comms`](../packs/use-the-stakeholder-comms-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Who is my audience and what rules should the deck follow?"
- "What are the structural rules for presenting to a board versus engineers?"
- "Profile this audience so I know how technical to go"
- "We have a mixed exec and technical room — how should I pitch it?"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Build the PowerPoint for the board meeting"
- "Outline the slides for this deck"
- "Write the one-page executive summary"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use audience-profile".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Profile output is concrete.** "Slide count: 8–12" beats "keep it short".
- **Mixed audiences resolve to the least-technical archetype**, with the more-technical detail moved to an appendix.
- **Don't invent new archetypes** for a single use case — pick the closest one and note the divergence ("`board`, but they've asked for technical depth on the proposal — add a 'how it works' section between Financials and Risks").

## Use something else when

- For peer engineering communication where the "audience" is just "another engineer reading the doc". The standard documentation style is fine.
- For purely internal artifacts (ADRs, runbooks) — those have their own conventions independent of audience.
